text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered - autoscaler ceiling reached for cluster: gpu-pool-3 (AutoscalerEvent: MAX_NODE_REACHED). Queue length for /v1/generate > 12k, average request latency spiking, ~40% 429 throttles. Link: https://internal.redwood/alerts/1755551234

Alex (oncall): acked. I'm taking this. oncall runbook step1: assess impact and try fallback routing.

Alex (oncall): Jin, can you confirm customer-facing errors? any big customers hit?

Jin (support): seeing a handful of high-traffic customers (acct: alpha-inc, beta-saas) with elevated 429 and 5xx logs since ~1755551100. Support is already fielding tickets.

Maria (eng-runtime): quick datapoints: node count is at maxNodes=48 (policy), cluster autoscaler reported scale-up blocked due to account limit. Pod backlog from k8s queue-proxy: pending pods ~820, pending GPU pod images pulling minimal. KV-cache warmups stalled.

Priya (sre): checking cloud quotas now. If this is an account-level vm limit we need a manual cap raise or temporary fallback to lower-tier models.

Sam (ops): I can do an emergency bump on reserved capacity if we decide. Need OK from product and safety checks. Will prepare commands.

Alex (oncall): safety checks: 1) ensure no hot pods causing eviction 2) confirm storage/network not bottleneck. Maria, run pod evictions and node unschedulable checks?

Maria (eng-runtime): running quick checks: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l
kubectl describe node | grep -E "Allocatable|MemoryPressure|DiskPressure"
```
No disk pressure, network fine. Pending reason: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu. Not node-level eviction.

Priya (sre): cloud quota: GPU vCPU quotas in us-west-2 are at quota cap for this account. Support ticket already open with cloud provider (ticket 789123). ETA unclear.

Alex (oncall): product impact assessment: Lewis, what's the severity for customers? any committed SLAs?

Lewis (product): multiple customers on paid tiers affected (severity: P1 for impacted flows). We should do manual capacity unlock now to mitigate. Also update status page.

Sam (ops): preparing manual override. Command below is internal tool (rwdctl) - I will not run until Alex authorizes.
```
rwdctl capacity bump --cluster gpu-pool-3 --add-nodes 8 --reason "emergency-autoscale-ceiling" --owner alex
```

Alex (oncall): do it. Confirm rollback plan after traffic drops. Priya - confirm we're not stepping over any safety guard (quotas aside).

Priya (sre): confirmed we have spare IPs and storage. Cloud budget alert will trigger but acceptable for emergency. Proceed.

Sam (ops): running now... :computer:

deploy-bot: starting temporary node provisioning workflow (run id: rf-202403-1755)

Sam (ops): nodes requested. AWS ASG scaling group updated to desired=56, pending instance launches.

Maria (eng-runtime): k8s nodes joining... kubelet bootstrap ok for 6 new nodes. Pod binder picking up backlog. Starting to drain the queue.

Alex (oncall): monitoring token-level errors. Pulling metrics: 429 rate beginning to fall from 40% -> 18% in last 4 min. Good sign.

Jin (support): updating customers: short note posted to status page and direct outreach to top 5 affected accounts.

Priya (sre): cloud provider ticket updated: we did manual bump; tagging cloud ops. Provider asked us to lower after peak.

Sam (ops): all requested nodes reported Ready. new node count 56. pods scheduling onto GPUs. backlog dropped from 820 -> 120 in ~6 min.

Alex (oncall): nice. Can we add a temporary routing policy to send new inference traffic to smaller models to avoid re-saturating? Maria?

Maria (eng-runtime): yes, I can flip fallback-policy in the gateway for 30m to route non-critical workloads to cpu-fallback or quantized model variants. Doing now: 
```
curl -XPOST https://internal.redwood/api/v1/route/modify -d '{"policy":"fallback-30m","match":"non-critical"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer **redacted**'
```

Maria (eng-runtime): fallback enabled. Expect lower GPU pressure.

Alex (oncall): great. Next steps: 1) let traffic stabilize, 2) monitor cost and SLA impact, 3) run post-incident RCA. Who will own RCA?

Lewis (product): I'll own the customer communication and product action items.

Priya (sre): I'll own infra RCA and quota action (raise request to cloud).

Sam (ops): I'll document the manual bump steps and create a runbook snippet to reduce time to mitigate next time.

Taylor (next-oncall): taking note for handoff in 20m. Please DM if anything flares up.

Alex (oncall): handoff: I'll remain until stabilization. If error rate < 2% for 15m, I'll mark mitigated.

Maria (eng-runtime): metrics: 429s now at 1.6%, median latency back to normal. Queue fully drained at 1755551350.

Alex (oncall): marking mitigated. Filing postmortem and linking runbook updates. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Priya (sre): follow-ups: - request quota increase with cloud provider - increase autoscaler maxNodes to 64 behind config flag with safety checks - add alert for pending pods > 200 for 5m.

Lewis (product): also discuss adding automatic degraded-mode routing in platform so we don't need manual flips.

Sam (ops): created ticket INFRA-4521 with steps + timestamps. Added owner: Sam.

IncidentBot: Incident resolved (duration ~7m). Logs archived: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1755551234/logs

Alex (oncall): closing thread. we'll post RCA tomorrow.
